acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
acceptance.verdict: Guide-following output hits nearly every rubric line verbatim (one policy table with placement/retryable/escalate columns, four consumer roles, tiered boundaries, single renderer owning session-escalation, explicit architecture-test diff touching only table+i18n) and correctly defers the wire envelope to error:format; isolated baseline is also strong (better on Apex bulk-failure/idempotency/correlation-id specifics) but never instantiates a concrete table, never names tiered boundaries or a single escalation owner, and offers no architecture-test proof.

checklist.note: Plain documentation aimed at humans/architecture guidance, no model-directive language.
No network calls or data transmission anywhere; skill has no scripts.
No credentials; only fictional/example reason codes like Pkg__RATE_LIMITED.
No scripts or shell commands exist in this skill (only SKILL.md).
All content is readable prose and plain pseudocode, nothing encoded.
No fetch/download logic present; skill is documentation only.
No reads of ~/.ssh, .env, or any credential store.
No sudo, cron, or persistence mechanisms; no executable content at all.
